### Observed differences

- In the later window, A32, A33 and A34 each occur in all 200 traces (100%), with about 1.0 occurrence per trace on average; before, each occurred in only about half of traces (52%, 48%, 48%) with about 0.5 occurrences per trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- A25's outgoing behaviour changed: before, about 99% of its transitions went to A26; after, about 49% go to A33 and 49% to A34, with A26 no longer a successor. [DIR001]
- A28's outgoing behaviour changed: before, about 52% went to A32, 26% to A34 and 21% to A33; after, about 98% go to A32. [DIR002]
- A33's outgoing behaviour changed: before, about 55% went to A29 and 44% to A34; after, about 48% go to A26 and 50% to A34, with A29 no longer a successor. [DIR003]
- A34's outgoing behaviour changed: before, about 54% went to A33 and 44% to A29; after, about 51% go to A26 and 48% to A33, with A29 no longer a successor. [DIR004]
- Order relations changed: before, A25 was immediately followed by A26 (lag 1 in 99% of cases); after, A26 is about 3 steps after A25, while A33 and A34 now occur shortly after A25 (lag 1–2) instead of later (lag 4–5). [LAG001, LAG003, LAG004]
- Before, A32 and A33/A34 were mutually exclusive: A32 appeared in about 52% of traces and A33/A34 in about 48%, never together. After, all three co-occur in every trace, with A33 and A34 occurring before A26, A28 and A32. [REL013, REL014, REL015, REL005, REL006, REL008, REL009]
- Position shifts agree: A33 and A34 moved earlier (mean position from about 0.53 to 0.44), while A26, A28 and A29 moved later (e.g., A26 from 0.43 to 0.49, A28 from 0.50 to 0.55). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS005, POS006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in which the process moved from two alternative branches — one containing A32 and one containing A33/A34 — to a single sequence where A33 and A34 occur early after A25, followed by A26, A28, A32 and A29. Specifically, A25 now routes to A33/A34 instead of A26, A28 now routes almost exclusively to A32, and A33/A34 now route to A26 instead of A29. The order changes are directly shown by relational and lag evidence, and the participation changes are consistent with the disappearance of the two-branch split. A competing explanation of sampling differences in variant frequencies cannot be fully excluded, but the large, consistent differences across occurrence, routing, position, relation and lag indicators make that unlikely. Some lag items in the later window rest on very few traces (e.g., A26–A33, A26–A34, A28–A33, A28–A34 each have support of 1 trace), so those specific lags are weak, but the main order relations are supported by hundreds of traces.
